pencereler.0-5: The SL-1 reactor exploded during maintenance. In an instant, all three men working on
pencereler.5-12: it were killed. They were reconnecting its central control rod. That rod had to be lifted by hand. It
pencereler.12-20: was pulled far too high. The reactor went critical and flashed water to steam. The blast lifted the reactor vessel off its
pencereler.20-30: mounts. Reactors were then designed so no single rod can do this.

segmentler.metin: The SL-1 reactor exploded during maintenance.
It took only a single control rod pulled out too far by hand.
So how could a single control rod pulled out too far by hand do this?
The answer is prompt criticality from manual withdrawal of the central control rod, causing a steam explosion — and it is why reactors were designed so no single rod can make them critical.
